articles.title: Kakinada fishermen who went missing docked at Vizag harbour, sold catch and sailed again before contact was lost
articles.summary: Hyderabad: Authorities have launched a sustained sea search for seven fishermen from Kakinada district who have been missing since November 14, deploying warships and helicopters in continuous operations. The men, from Subbampeta village in Uppada mandal, left the Uppada coast on November 4 for a fishing voyage. They docked at Visakhapatnam Fishing Harbour on November 10, sold their catch and set sail again the same day. They stayed in phone contact with their families until November 14, after which all communication ceased. The Indian Coast Guard found that the boat was last spotted near Paradip Port in Odisha on November 18, after which it 'disappeared'. Kakinada District Collector M N Harendhira Prasad said on Wednesday that the district administration received information on the evening of November 19 that the fishermen were missing. The administration went on alert immediately and informed the Coast Guard. No information has been available from the men, either by phone or through the boat's transponder. Seven fishermen found safe in stranded boat off Kakinada coast: Andhra Minister Kakinada Coast Guard officials responded at once and intensified search operations. Information was passed to the Odisha and Chennai Coast Guard centres, and coordination was established among the departments concerned. The Coast Guard and Navy are jointly conducting an extensive search, which is continuing at sea without a break, he said. Details of the incident have also been shared with the naval authorities of Bangladesh and Myanmar. Officials are working to gather more information on the missing men and trace their final movements, using available surveillance and communication systems to pinpoint their location. The Collector expressed hope that the seven men would return safely. He said the search would continue, in coordination with the officials concerned, until their whereabouts are found. Deputy Chief Minister Pawan Kalyan also reviewed the situation with the Collector. He directed that the search be intensified further and said that, with the cooperation of the Marine Police, Coast Guard and Navy, every inch of the sea should be combed. He asked the Collector to monitor the operations continuously and keep him informed, and said every possible effort should be made to rescue the fishermen. Pawan Kalyan assured the families that the coalition government would make every effort to bring the men back safely and urged them not to be anxious. In another incident, seven fishermen who had gone fishing from Yetimoga in Kakinada district and were stranded on a boat with engine failure have been brought back safely, Agriculture Minister Kinjarapu Atchannaidu said. The boat was stranded about 3 km from the shore, near Krishnapuram on the Uppada–Tuni coast. As the water there is shallow, the fishermen were brought ashore with the help of another boat.

articles.title: Woman accuses Assam deputy speaker, BJP leader of fathering her child and then abandoning her
articles.summary: Diphu, Assam: A woman from Assam's Karbi Anglong has alleged that state assembly Deputy Speaker Dr Habbey Teron fathered her child, but did not marry her as promised and distanced himself from her after being elected an MLA earlier this year. She demanded that Teron undergo a DNA test to prove paternity of her son. Teron, a first-time BJP MLA, was not available for comment, while Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma said, without elaborating, that he could not intervene in this matter as traditional customary laws are in force in Karbi Anglong. The woman claimed that she came in contact with Teron, who represents the Amri (ST) constituency, during the COVID-19 pandemic when he provided her with medical treatment. Assam is rocking, best is yet to come: CM Himanta gives Guns N' Roses twist to state's achievements She claimed Teron had promised her marriage, following which she ended her relationship with her previous husband and began living with him in a rented house in Guwahati. Subsequently, a son was born to the woman, who also has another child with her husband. The woman said she was willing to undergo a DNA test to establish the paternity of her five-year-old son and challenged Teron to agree to the test. She alleged that after Teron became an MLA and later deputy speaker of the assembly, he began to avoid her, evicted her from the rented accommodation, and had security personnel send her away. The woman said attempts to meet him were unsuccessful and security personnel were deployed to prevent her from approaching him. She also alleged that cases had been filed against her through other individuals at Teron's instance to harass her. The woman on Tuesday appealed to Assam Assembly Speaker Ranjeet Kumar Dass, Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma and the police to intervene in the matter and ensure justice for her. The chief minister, on the sidelines of a programme on Wednesday, said he had noticed the allegations against Teron on social media. ''The Karbi society is governed by its own customary laws, but there is also the law of the land. There is nothing the chief minister can say in this matter. We will abide by what the law says,'' Sarma said. BJP's Assam Pradesh Minority Morcha in-charge Numal Momin said that a DNA test is the ultimate solution to prove someone's innocence or guilt. "Unless proved otherwise, no character assassination, please," Momin, the deputy speaker in the previous assembly, said in a social media post. Assam college rolls back advisory asking PG doctors to defer 'personal milestones' as marriage amid outrage Meanwhile, Teron was unavailable for comment, and his phone remained switched off since Tuesday. Assam Pradesh Mahila Congress president Mira Borthakur Goswami, in a letter to the chief minister, demanded an impartial, time-bound investigation into the allegations against Teron. She requested the CM to ensure that the principles and laws regarding women's dignity and protection apply equally to all. Goswami also demanded Teron’s resignation within 24 hours and urged the police to register a suo motu case against him based on the woman’s allegations.

articles.title: KPSC scam: Karnataka High Court orders SIT probe into ED-flagged recruitment irregularities
articles.summary: Bengaluru: The Karnataka High Court has directed the Special Investigation Team (SIT) to probe the instances of irregularities and malpractices in KPSC recruitments detected by the Enforcement Directorate (ED). On November 19, the ED shared the information with the SIT about discrepancies it found in the recruitment of Assistant Executive Engineers in Rural Drinking Water and Sanitation department, KAS Gazetted Officers exam - 2023, Motor Vehicle Inspectors recruitment examination of 2016 and Assistant Engineer recruitment exam of the BBMP. KPSC 'scam': Ex-chairman, member in judicial custody The SIT is presently investigating the Veterinary Officers recruitment scam. After perusing the status report submitted by the ED, Justice M Nagaprasanna said the revelations in the status report are shocking. “If the revelations in the status report were to ultimately bear the imprimatur of truth, they would have a chilling effect on the credibility of the entire recruitment process undertaken by the KPSC,” the court said, adding that this subsequent development, and the material surfaced in the ED investigation, cannot be viewed in isolation or through the narrow prism of the two crimes that initially occasioned the constitution of the SIT. The court further said, “The nature of the allegations is such that it would shock not merely the conscience of this Court, but equally the conscience of every ordinary citizen who, with an abiding faith in the fairness of the system, participates in the recruitment processes conducted by the KPSC, year after year, across various disciplines. The information so shared cannot be permitted to remain a mere exchange of correspondence between two investigating agencies. It must receive the requisite statutory response and be taken to its logical conclusion in accordance with law.” The court further extended the interim orders granted to the petitioners, who are successful candidates, observing that no coercive steps should be taken against them till the next date of hearing, subject to the petitioners extending their fullest cooperation with the investigation, either at the hands of the ED or the SIT. The court further directed both the SIT and ED to submit their respective updated status reports while adjourning the hearing in the batch of petitions to January 8, 2027.

articles.title: Bengal CM Suvendu Adhikari claims ex-Prez Pranab Mukherjee advised him to leave TMC, join PM Modi
articles.summary: Kolkata: West Bengal Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari on Wednesday claimed that former President Pranab Mukherjee had advised him to leave the TMC and align with Prime Minister Narendra Modi if he wanted to carve out an independent political career, as he would otherwise remain an "employee" in the Mamata Banerjee-led party. Speaking to reporters on the sidelines of the Ras Mela in Cooch Behar, Adhikari declined to elaborate on this, saying he did not want any further discussion on the late Congress leader, whom he described as a "great personality". Adhikari, once a prominent TMC leader and a minister in the Mamata Banerjee government, joined the BJP in December 2020, ahead of the West Bengal Assembly elections. "Pranab babu has gone to the abode of God. He is no longer among us. He was a great personality. He is a revered figure, and I do not want any unnecessary discussion on this," the chief minister said. TMC govt considered only Muslims as minority: West Bengal CM Suvendu Adhikari Adhikari's remarks came a day after he recalled how Mukherjee had advised him to leave the TMC, where he felt he would remain an "employee" of the party leadership, and work with Modi if he wished to advance independently in politics. Speaking at an Economic Times event in Kolkata on Tuesday night, Adhikari had described the TMC as a party controlled by former chief minister Mamata Banerjee and her nephew Abhishek Banerjee, likening its functioning to a privately run company with a chairman and managing director. "I was also there (in the TMC), but I did not want to remain an employee. That is why I walked out," he had said, referring to his decision to leave the TMC in 2020. The chief minister had described Mukherjee as his "original adviser" and recalled visiting him at Rashtrapati Bhavan after he became President. According to Adhikari, Mukherjee had then advised him to consider whether he wanted to continue working under the TMC leadership or pursue his political ambitions independently by aligning with Modi. "If you want to remain an employee, stay with her. If you want to move ahead on your own strength, stay with Modi ji," Adhikari had quoted Mukherjee as telling him. The chief minister, however, had refrained from specifying when the conversation took place, saying he did not wish to invite controversy over the words of a leader who was no longer alive. Mukherjee, who served as India's president from 2012 to 2017, was a senior Congress leader and one of the country's most experienced political figures. After joining the BJP, Adhikari subsequently became the Leader of the Opposition in the state Assembly after the party's defeat in the 2021 polls. He became the chief minister after the BJP's landslide victory in the 2026 Assembly elections. The BJP won 208 of the 294 Assembly seats, while the TMC secured 80, marking the end of its 15-year rule in the state. Mamata Banerjee lost the Bhabanipur constituency to Adhikari.

A three-month long drive that made Keralam's Wayanad e-waste free
articles.summary: Thiruvananthapuram: A hardly three-months long drive at the ecologically fragile Wayanad district of Keralam has resulted in collecting over 100 tons of e-waste, thereby making the district the first e-waste free district in the country. Chief Minister V D Satheesan will be making a formal announcement in this regard on Friday. The district is also launching a plastic-free drive as part of the long term goal of making the district carbon neutral and preserving the bio diversity. Keralam's Wayanad set to become India's first e-waste-free district It was in September that the drive to collect e-waste was launched in the district. Spearheaded by state government agency Suchitwa Mission, the drive was initially carried out at around 180 government institutions in the district. Later door-to-door collection from homes and other establishments by the local bodies in the district was carried out. E-waste collection centres were also set up and complaint numbers were published for people to seek help in handing over e-waste. Suchitwa mission programme officer Anoop K said that the initial response itself was very positive as 32 tonnes of e-waste could be collected from the government offices in the first phase of the drive itself. A total of 102.8 tons of e-waste were so far collected. Subsequently door to door collection was carried out with the support of local self government institutions in the district. People were made aware of the serious ecological threats posed by the heavy metals in e-waste, especially pollution caused to water bodies and soil. Those engaged in the collection, mostly Haritha Karma Sena volunteers, were also given proper training on handling the e-waste. The Clean Kerala Company hands over the e-waste to government approved recycling companies. Initially each local body wards were declared e-waste free after verification by the respective ward members and local body authorities. Once all the wards in a local body were declared e-waste free that local body was declared e-waste free and finally the entire district attained the e-waste free status. The entire e-waste collected was handed over to the Clean Kerala Company, an agency under the state government that handles the solid waste. In order to ensure that the district remains e-waste free, similar drives would be carried out every three months. Agriculture minister and local MLA T Siddique and local self government minister K M Shaji have been personally supervising the drive. Siddique said that a drive to make the district plastic free would be launched. To begin with, all the tourist spots in the district would be initially made plastic free, he said.

articles.title: Allahabad High Court stays FIR over AI-generated audio clip for violation of settled law
articles.summary: Lucknow: The Allahabad High Court on Wednesday stayed an FIR registered against a man for allegedly sharing an AI-generated audio clip on Facebook, and observed that Uttar Pradesh authorities were repeatedly "jumping the gun" by lodging criminal defamation cases in violation of settled law. A division bench of Justice Abdul Moin and Justice Pramod Kumar Srivastava at Lucknow directed the additional chief secretary (Home) to file a personal affidavit explaining why FIRs were being registered under Section 356 (defamation) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), 2023, despite a 2016 Supreme Court judgement laying down the procedure for initiating criminal defamation proceedings. The court also asked the senior official to explain what action was proposed against officials who continued to disregard the apex court's ruling. It warned that if the affidavit was not filed by the next date of hearing, the ACS (Home) would have to appear personally along with the relevant records, according to the order. Allahabad High Court pulls up Uttar Pradesh government over registration of FIRs under law declared 'stillborn' by top court The order was passed on a writ petition filed by Mohd Riyaz alias Riyaz Gazi, who challenged an FIR registered on October 29, 2026, at Kotwali Police Station in Hardoi under Section 356 of the BNS and Section 66D of the Information Technology Act. According to the FIR, the petitioner had shared on his Facebook wall a post uploaded by another person, Dilshad Khan, containing an allegedly AI-generated and edited audio clip. The complainant, stated to be a mandal president of a political party, alleged that the post had tarnished his image and that of the party. The petitioner contended that merely sharing someone else's post did not attract Section 66D of the IT Act and alleged that the FIR was malicious and an abuse of the legal process. Opposing the plea, the state argued that the offences were made out as the petitioner had shared an edited post. The bench, however, observed prima facie that Section 66D of the IT Act dealt with cheating by personation using a computer resource. The FIR did not disclose any instance of the petitioner cheating someone by personation, it noted. On the charge of criminal defamation, the bench relied on a 2016 Supreme Court judgement which held that proceedings for defamation must be initiated through a complaint case by the aggrieved person and not through an FIR. The court also noted that Section 222 of the BNS provides for the initiation of defamation proceedings through a complaint by the person aggrieved. In view of these observations, the bench stayed the operation of the FIR until further orders and fixed December 15 as the next date of hearing.

articles.title: Imphal witnessed most intense earthquakes: IIT Guwahati study on 6,000 quakes across seismically active Northeastern region
articles.summary: Guwahati: Manipur capital Imphal had recorded the most intense level of ground shaking during earthquakes, says a research team from Indian Institute of Technology, Guwahati (IIT-G) that studied 6,000 earthquakes witnessed in the seismically active Northeastern region. The research team, headed by Abhishek Kumar, a professor in the department of civil engineering, compiled information on earthquakes that occurred over the past 1,200 years to produce a catalogue containing records of nearly 6,000 earthquakes. They created 200 synthetic earthquake catalogues by varying earthquake locations and magnitudes within specified uncertainty ranges. A statistical sampling method called Latin Hypercube Sampling was used for this process. The researchers then combined these estimates with mathematical models to calculate potential ground shaking in eight cities, Guwahati, Agartala, Imphal, Shillong, Aizawl, Kohima, Gangtok and Itanagar. The team that used a measurement called Peak Ground Acceleration found that Imphal had the highest estimated level of ground shaking among the eight cities studied. Explained | What makes earthquakes so deadly? The most intense earthquake activity is seen in the Indo-Burma Ranges, followed by western Arunachal Pradesh, central Assam, the Shillong Plateau and southern Sikkim, the IIT Guwahati said on Wednesday. "This information, along with site-specific assessments like soil structure, could help engineers and construction specialists design earthquake-resistant structures," it said. Significant study The study is seen as important given that the Northeast India lies between two tectonic boundaries and contains the Shillong Plateau and many geological faults, all of which make it prone to earthquakes. The 1897 Shillong earthquake and the 1950 Assam earthquake caused massive devastation to the region. The team said currently the seismic hazard assessment is carried out based on information about previous earthquakes and geological faults to estimate how strongly the ground could shake during a future earthquake. Two earthquakes hit northwestern Nepal But earthquake activity is not uniform in the Northeast and historical data is not always accurate because of the absence of modern measurement devices in the past. The team, therefore, developed a method that takes the uncertainties into account when estimating seismic hazards, said the IITG. "We used a mathematical technique called Kernel Density Estimation that considers the local differences in earthquake occurrence. We also considered the orientation of the geological faults because earthquake activity is more likely to occur along a fault than in other areas," Kumar said. The findings of the research have been published in the Journal of Seismology. As the next step, the research team now plans to incorporate depth-related uncertainties and an earthquake recurrence model into the proposed framework. These enhancements are expected to provide a more comprehensive representation of seismicity, improve the robustness of probabilistic seismic hazard estimates, and further strengthen the applicability of the proposed methodology for seismic hazard assessment in North-East India, the IITG said.

articles.title: New anaemia data raise questions over progress of Anaemia Mukt Bharat
articles.summary: Months after releasing the latest National Family Health Survey (NFHS) factsheet without crucial data on anaemia, the Union government has finally published the figures under a separate study. They were released on Tuesday, November 24, in a study titled the Survey for Assessment of Markers of Population Health, Activity, Diet and Anthropometry (SAMPADA) 2023–2025. The data show that nearly 56% of women of reproductive age (15-49 years) are anaemic, despite a systematic intervention through Anaemia Mukt Bharat (AMB), a strategy launched in 2018. The Union Ministry, however, said that severe anaemia was observed only in less than 2% of people in the majority of the age groups. The report was prepared by the Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR) under the Union Ministry of Health and Family Welfare. While the government claimed that the prevalence of anaemia came down, experts point out that results of SAMPADA are not comparable with previous national surveys. An analysis of the Union Government’s scheme Anaemia Mukt Bharat, in the backdrop of survey results, shows nearly half of the funds remain unutilised. The Anaemia Mukt Bharat strategy, launched in 2018, aimed to reduce anaemia among children, adolescents, pregnant and lactating women and women of reproductive age through various interventions, including the distribution of iron folic acid supplements. Anaemia figures show decline, but… The World Health Organisation (WHO) defines anaemia as a condition in which the number of red blood cells or the haemoglobin concentration within them is lower than normal, reducing the blood's capacity to carry oxygen to the body's tissues. According to the WHO, it is diagnosed when blood haemoglobin levels fall below specific thresholds set by age, sex, and physiological status. Anaemia is a serious global public health problem that particularly affects young children, menstruating adolescent girls and women, and pregnant and postpartum women. As per the new study, the prevalence of anaemia in children aged 12-59 months is 42%. Adolescent girls aged 10-19 years had an anaemia prevalence of 46%; adolescent boys aged 10-19 years and men aged 20-59 years had 22-23%, whereas women of reproductive age had 56% prevalence. The NFHS 4 recorded a prevalence of anaemia in children (age 6-59 months) as 58%, women (age 15-49 years) as 53.2%, and pregnant women (15-49 years) as 50.4%. However, all these figures went up in the NFHS-5, with children (age 6-59 months) recording 67%, women (age 15-49 years) at 57%, and pregnant women (15-49 years) at 52.2%. This invited intense criticism, with many pointing it out as a failure of the AMB strategy and Poshan Abhiyaan, which aimed to overcome nutritional deficiencies. A statement by the Union Ministry on November 24 said that there was an ‘encouraging shift’ with overall lower prevalence of anaemia compared to previous studies. It claimed a reduction in anaemia prevalence compared to previous surveys. However, experts said it is difficult to compare SAMPADA findings with NFHS over the difference in method of sampling and age group. While the SAMPADA study has taken the adolescent age category between 10 and 19 years, it was between 15 and 19 for NFHS. The SAMPADA used venous blood sampling instead of NFHS’ capillary finger-prick tests. Removed from NFHS 6 Following criticism over higher prevalence of anaemia in NFHS 4 and 5, the government decided to drop anaemia prevalence figures from the next NFHS, citing that capillary finger-prick tests used by NFHS overestimated the prevalence of anaemia. The factsheet of NFHS 6, released in May this year, omitted crucial data such as anaemia and sex ratio for the first time since its launch in 1992-93. Instead of capillary finger-prick tests, the SAMPADA used venous blood sampling and automated analysers for haemoglobin estimation, which, according to the Health Ministry, provided greater accuracy and reproducibility. In a capillary test, blood is drawn from a prick made on finger tips, while venous blood sampling involves collecting blood from a vein using a syringe. Comparing the SAMPADA survey with NHFS-5, the Ministry said that the anaemia prevalence in children, women, men and pregnant women dropped 25.2 percentage points (pp) in children, 1 pp in women, 6 pp in men and 8 pp in pregnant women. Public health expert Dr Sylvia Karpagam told TNM that the results of capillary finger-prick test in NFHS and venous blood sampling methods in SAMPADA are not comparable. “Compared to NFHS, SAMPADA’s sample population is small. The benefit of the capillary method is that it can be compared with previous surveys and international standards. For venous, you need a trained lab technician, draw blood, etc., while the other involves just a prick,” she said. Dr Sylvia said that removing the capillary finger-prick test and anaemia prevalence from NFHS data were deliberate. SAMPADA results said that 1.7 lakh blood samples were taken. Though the exact number of blood samples taken is not mentioned in NFHS, the previous one (NFHS-5) had interviewed 7 lakh women and over 1 lakh men. The Union Ministry’s statement also said that vitamin B12 and folate deficiency have limited contribution to anaemia in India, as their prevalence was similar in both anaemic and non-anaemic individuals across population groups. Dr Sylvia said the fact that B12 deficiency exists itself is a serious issue. “The prevalence of B12 deficiency had been high during pre-Covid studies, and it definitely should have increased,” she said. Gap in AMB fund utilisation The AMB, which devised various strategies, including the supply of iron and folic acid supplements among target groups, testing, awareness, etc., to beat anaemia, had so far spent over Rs 2,534.97 crore during the period from 2021-22 to 2024-25. A reply in Lok Sabha in March 2026 shows that there has been a sharp drop in the funds earmarked for the project after 2021-22. There is also a huge gap between the approved funds and its expenditure. If 73.23% of funds were spent in 2021-22, it dropped to just 33.76 % the next year. Only 38.93 % of the total allocated money of Rs 809 crore was spent in 2024-25. The average fund utilisation rate is 52.82 %, showing a gap of Rs 2,264.43 crore between approved funds and expenditure. The expenditure figure includes spending from central funds released, the corresponding State share, and unspent balances carried forward from the previous year. Releasing the survey, the Union Health ministry said that SAMPADA provided comprehensive national evidence to further strengthen Anaemia Mukt Bharat. “It is encouraging that prevalence of anaemia is lower in SAMPADA compared to previous national surveys. The comprehensive anaemia profiling in the SAMPADA survey provides an evidence base to strengthen the ongoing national efforts towards Anaemia Mukt Bharat,” said Dr Rajiv Bahl, Secretary, Department of Health Research, and DG, ICMR, in a statement.

articles.title: 18 years after 26/11 Mumbai attacks, memories and scars lives on
articles.summary: Mumbai: Eighteen years after the 2008 terror attacks that shook Mumbai and exposed glaring lacunae in India's security and intelligence apparatus, the horrors of the 60-hour assault and bloodletting remain etched in public memory. As the financial capital, know for its unbreakable spirit and courage in the face of adversity, prepares to commemorate the 18th anniversary of 26/11, the carnage remains a grim reminder of the human cost of terrorism and the importance of sustained vigilance and preparedness against security threats. The November 26, 2008 attacks, carried out by 10 heavily armed Lashkar-e-Taiba (LeT) terrorists who sailed into Mumbai from Pakistan, left 166 people, including foreigners, dead and more than 300 injured, making it one of the deadliest terror strikes in an Indian city. Mumbai has endured several major terrorist attacks over the past three decades or so. On March 12, 1993, bomb blasts struck 12 locations in the megapolis killing 257 and injuring thousands. The city reeled under the serial train blasts on July 11, 2006, killing 188 people, while 27 people died in triple explosions at Dadar, Zaveri Bazaar and Opera House on July 13, 2011. Eighteen years after 26/11 terror attacks, Ajmal Kasab's lawyers still await fees The 2008 attacks, which began on the night of November 26 and continued until the morning of November 29, targeted several prominent locations, including the Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Terminus (CSMT), the Taj Mahal Palace Hotel, the Trident Hotel, Nariman House (Chabad House), Leopold Cafe and Cama and Albless Hospital. The heavily armed terrorists launched coordinated attacks, taking hostages and engaging security personnel in prolonged gun battles. The operations posed enormous challenges as the attackers occupied buildings, used their height and layout to their advantage and held people hostage. The coordinated response by the Mumbai Police, armed police personnel, Indian Navy's Marine Commandos and the National Security Guard (NSG) eventually brought the roughly 60-hours siege to an end. The sea-borne attacks exposed vulnerabilities in coastal security, intelligence gathering and coordination among security agencies, prompting a major overhaul of India's counter-terrorism preparedness. Among the 10 attackers, Mohammed Ajmal Kasab was captured alive. He was subsequently tried, convicted and hanged in November 2012. David Coleman Headley, one of the key conspirators who conducted reconnaissance of Mumbai before the attacks, later deposed before an Indian court through video-conferencing from the United States. Tahawwur Hussain Rana, another accused in the 26/11 conspiracy, was extradited from the US in 2025 to stand trial in India. However, several masterminds and handlers of the attacks continue to remain beyond India's reach, with many believed to be based in Pakistan. The chargesheet filed in the case had stated that the manner in which the attacks were conducted showed they were meticulously planned and executed after extensive training, preparation and briefing. 26/11 aftermath: Maharashtra Police draft drone-use policy for Mumbai, other key cities The attacks prompted global condemnation and led to significant changes in India's counter-terrorism measures. Every year floral tributes are paid at the Mumbai Police headquarters to those who made the ultimate sacrifice while fighting terrorists during the attacks. Homage is also paid at Mumbai CSMT, Cama and Albless Hospital and other locations which were targeted by the Pakistani terrorists. Mumbaikars also gather at "Prerana Sthal", the statue of Assistant Sub-Inspector Tukaram Ombale, who fought with terrorists with a lathi and was killed while catching the terrorist Kasab at Girgaon Chowpatty in south Mumbai.

articles.title: 'Don't force it': Supreme Court clarifies students opted for three languages under CBSE policy can continue
articles.summary: New Delhi: The Supreme Court on Wednesday clarified that students who have already chosen three languages under the CBSE’s three-language policy may continue with those choices and need not switch back to two languages under the transitional relaxation granted earlier. A bench of Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana made the observation while hearing a batch of petitions challenging the CBSE formula. Senior advocate Gopal Sankaranarayanan appeared for the petitioners and Solicitor General Tushar Mehta for the CBSE. Students of Classes 7, 8 and 9 remain exempt from the full three-language requirement , under which at least two languages must be native Indian languages. They can continue with two foreign languages and one Indian language, with the third language assessed only at the school level and not through a board examination. Supreme Court inclined to stay Calcutta High Court order delaying KMC polls The court had earlier questioned the characterisation of English as a “non-native” language and sought details on infrastructural preparedness, without staying the policy. The CBSE had approached the court seeking modification of its September 28 order. That order directed the board to consider extending to Class 6 students the same transitional relaxation available to Class 7 students. The board contended that the exemption for Classes 6 to 9 needed reconsideration because some students had already opted for three-language combinations. Considering the matter, the bench said, “Our direction was that students of Class 6, if they have opted for three languages, they will continue for three languages. If they have not opted, don’t force them… let them continue in the way they are continuing.” The bench further said that where two languages are already being studied, students will be allowed to continue with two languages this year, subject to taking up the third language next year. “This is a human problem… Those who have already opted, very good. Then those students will continue,” the court said, assuring that those who chose three languages would not be required to revert. When the Solicitor General urged that the relaxation should not extend until Class 10, Justice Bagchi noted that Class 7 student has already been given the exception up to Class 10 and asked the board to examine the position. Supreme Court flags political influence in criminal prosecution in Senthil Balaji cash-for-jobs case Senior advocate Sankaranarayanan lopposed any modification order without hearing the petitioners. The court clarified that the bench only intended to ensure continuity as those continuing with two languages may do so, and those who opted for three languages should be allowed to persist with them. Institutions should not reverse the choices of students who had already selected three languages. articles.title: 128 kmph to zero: Train crew averts major disaster amid massive OHE failure in West Bengal
articles.summary: New Delhi: The running crew of the Shabd Bhedi Express averted a major disaster on November 19 between Howrah and Barddhaman in West Bengal , after the overhead equipment, which supplies electricity to the locomotive, collapsed and its wires became entangled with the train running at 128 kmph, officials said on Wednesday. Officials said the incident occurred around 11 pm amid extremely heavy rainfall, when the loco pilot and his assistant loco pilot noticed an abnormal situation despite poor visibility. They acted swiftly by applying emergency brakes, bringing the train to a halt from 128 kmph before the situation could escalate into a major disaster. The Shabd Bhedi Express is a weekly train that operates between Kolkata Chitpur in West Bengal and Ghazipur City in Uttar Pradesh. NGO, alumni object Railways quarters near Vontikoppal School in Mysuru "While Train No 22323 was running at approximately 128 kmph, it suddenly encountered a serious OHE entanglement situation. At around 23:00 hrs, amid extremely heavy rainfall, the loco pilot observed the contact wire violently waving ahead within the available visibility distance," an official said. The overhead equipment (OHE) system comprises several components, including the contact wire, which supplies electricity to the locomotive through its pantograph, the catenary wire, which supports the contact wire, and the cantilever structure, among others. "Recognising the imminent danger, the loco pilot immediately applied the emergency brake, bringing the train to a complete halt within approximately 1 km, from a speed of 128 kmph to zero," he added. Railways spent 80% of gross budgetary support in first three quarters of current fiscal Officials familiar with the incident said the situation was extremely critical and potentially disastrous. "The catenary wire had become detached and entangled with the wheels and body of the train. Furthermore, the structural and support arrangements, including the two-track cantilever structure, were found hanging, with OHE wires damaged over an approximate stretch of 2 km," the official said. "The incident had the potential to cause a catastrophic accident, involving extensive damage to the locomotive, coaches and railway infrastructure, with possible loss of precious human lives," he added. Fortunately, owing to the exceptional alertness, presence of mind and immediate emergency response of the train crew, a much bigger disaster was averted, officials said. They added that the locomotive was also saved from direct entanglement with the OHE equipment, while only the glass panes of a few coaches reportedly sustained damage. According to loco pilot unions, the incident once again highlights the importance of the train crew's alertness, professional competence, sound judgement and prompt decision-making in ensuring railway safety, particularly during extreme weather conditions and abnormal operating situations. "The timely action of the loco pilot deserves due recognition and appreciation. It is a remarkable example of how professional alertness and an appropriate emergency response can prevent a potentially catastrophic railway accident," a senior loco pilot said.

articles.summary: Lucknow: The Uttar Pradesh Special Task Force (STF) has arrested an alleged gang leader wanted in a case of cheating people on the pretext of sending them to Russia for construction jobs, officials said on Wednesday. Pankaj Nishad alias Golu, carrying a reward of Rs 50,000, was arrested near Nagarpur crossing under Jalalpur police station limits in Ambedkar Nagar district on Tuesday evening, the STF said in a statement. Nishad, a resident of Jaldipur village under Pawai police station limits in Azamgarh district, was wanted in a case registered at Tarun police station in Ayodhya in 2024 under sections relating to cheating, impersonation and forgery. According to the STF, the gang allegedly used online directory platform Justdial to identify and lure people looking for employment opportunities abroad. Its members had registered their contact numbers on the platform and posed as overseas recruitment agents when prospective job seekers called them. Man posing as CBI officer dupes Pune senior citizen of Rs 22 lakh on threat of 'digital arrest' The accused allegedly collected Rs 40,000 initially from each applicant after taking their passport, followed by another Rs 1.20 lakh after promising to arrange a visa and air ticket. They told the applicants that they would be sent to Russia on work visas for construction jobs, with a promised monthly salary of 4.5 lakh to 5 lakh Russian roubles, the STF said. The gang allegedly operated in collaboration with a company identified as JS Interference Limited, whose CEO was named as Sachin Singh in the statement. The accused told investigators that they paid Rs 1 lakh to the company as part of the arrangement. "Even after collecting the initial amounts, the gang allegedly demanded an additional Rs 1 lakh to Rs 2 lakh from the applicants. Those who refused to pay were sent fake flight-holding tickets to make them believe that their travel arrangements were underway," the STF said, quoting the accused. The arrest was made following intelligence inputs received by an STF team on Tuesday night, the agency said. During questioning, Nishad also disclosed that he had cases registered against him at different police stations and had earlier been arrested in a case registered at Dostpur police station in Sultanpur district in 2021, the STF said. The accused has been handed over to the Ayodhya police in connection with the 2024 case, and further legal proceedings will be carried out by the local police, it added.

However, following the case against him, he has been absconding. articles.title: Shapoor Mistry lobbied PM Modi twice for Tata Sons IPO as battle over listing intensifies
articles.summary: Mumbai: Shapoor Mistry, chairman of the Shapoorji Pallonji (SP) Group, twice approached Prime Minister Narendra Modi seeking intervention to push for a stock market listing of Tata Sons , exposing the deepening fault lines within India's most prominent business conglomerate over ownership, control and the future of its holding company. The appeals, made in October 2025 and June 2026, came as the debt-laden Shapoorji Pallonji (SP) Group sought to unlock value from its 18.37 per cent stake in Tata Sons, while the holding company's controlling shareholder, Tata Trusts, resisted a public offering. The correspondence, disclosed in an investigation by Mint based on Right to Information (RTI) responses from the Reserve Bank of India (RBI), also reveals extensive engagement between senior Tata executives and the central bank over the regulatory status and listing obligations of Tata Sons. The disclosure adds another dimension to the ongoing feud at the conglomerate, where Tata Trusts chairman Noel Tata has openly challenged the Tata Sons board's decision to pursue a listing as well as the reappointment of chairman N Chandrasekaran for another five-year term. The developments have exposed an unusual divide between the chairman of the holding company's controlling shareholder and the majority of its own board, bringing questions of ownership, governance, leadership and regulatory compliance into direct conflict. RBI reiterates demand for listing of Tata Sons According to Mint's RTI investigation, Shapoor Mistry wrote to Modi on October 24, 2025, seeking his intervention in the prolonged impasse over Tata Sons' listing. In an email titled "A Deepawali Letter of Faith, Hope, and Dharma - Request for appointment", he wrote: "In this spirit of Diwali when light triumphs over shadow, I humbly draw your attention to an issue that calls for your intervention on grounds of fairness and dharma the long-standing impasse concerning Tata Sons." Mistry accused Tata Trusts of holding Tata Sons "hostage for power and personal interest" and said the "height of adharma" had been reached because of what he alleged were violations of RBI rules and missed listing deadlines. He wrote to the prime minister again on June 12, 2026. The RBI provided Mint with the cover letter of the second communication but withheld its contents, citing business confidentiality provisions under Section 8(1)(d) of the RTI Act. There is no indication in the documents disclosed to Mint that the Prime Minister's Office responded to Mistry's appeals or granted him an audience. The October 2025 letter was forwarded to the Finance Ministry's Department of Financial Services, which sought the views of RBI deputy governors Shirish Chandra Murmu and Swaminathan J. The June 2026 communication was also routed through the department to the central bank. The RTI response further lists 16 meetings between senior RBI officials and Tata Group representatives between September 2022 and October 2026. Tata Sons chairman Chandrasekaran met former RBI governor Shaktikanta Das nine times, including twice in March 2024, shortly before the company applied to surrender its core investment company registration. He also met current governor Sanjay Malhotra in March 2025. Noel met Das on October 9, 2024, the day Ratan Tata died, and subsequently met Malhotra on April 29, 2026. Deputy Governor Murmu met Tata Group company secretary Suprakash Mukhopadhyay four times this year, including on October 28, between Tata Sons' request for regulatory guidance and the RBI's latest communication on listing. The frequency of these meetings underscores the sustained engagement between the Tata Group and the central bank as the company sought to avoid a public offering. The disclosures, however, do not establish that the meetings influenced the RBI's decisions. The regulatory dispute dates to September 2022, when the RBI classified Tata Sons as an upper-layer non-banking financial company (NBFC-UL), bringing it within a more stringent regulatory framework that requires such entities to list their shares within three years of identification. The original compliance deadline was September 30, 2025. Seeking to avoid the requirement, Tata Sons repaid more than Rs 21,000 crore in debt and applied in March 2024 to surrender its registration as a core investment company, arguing that it should no longer be subject to the regulatory classification that triggers mandatory listing. The application remained pending for about 29 months before the RBI rejected it on September 11, 2026, without publicly disclosing detailed reasons. Tata Sons had assets of about Rs 2.01 lakh crore as of March 31, 2026, substantially above the Rs 1 lakh crore threshold under the revised regulatory framework. In June 2026, the RBI had replaced its earlier scoring-based approach for identifying upper-layer NBFCs with an asset-size threshold. Jimmy Tata accuses Noel of seeking 'back-door takeover' of Tata Sons, calls for listing The central bank reinforced its position in a November 16 communication to Tata Sons chief financial officer Saurabh Agrawal, advising the company to comply with applicable regulations, explicitly including the listing requirement. The letter followed a request for regulatory guidance made by Tata Sons on October 6. The RBI's latest communication has significantly narrowed the scope for Tata Sons to continue resisting a listing through its existing regulatory arguments. The regulatory pressure coincided with a growing confrontation between Noel and the majority of the Tata Sons board. At its September 17 meeting, the board backed a move towards listing Tata Sons in compliance with RBI requirements and approved Chandrasekaran's reappointment for another five-year term beginning February 2027. The reappointment resolution was approved by a 4:1 vote, with Noel dissenting. He also opposed the listing proposal. Noel has been advocating an alternative to a public offering. His proposal involves merging Tata Electronics Systems Solutions and Tata Consulting Engineers into Tata Sons, with the objective of changing the holding company's regulatory classification and potentially taking it outside the framework that requires an upper-layer NBFC to list. Whether such a restructuring would actually secure an exemption remains subject to the RBI's assessment. The disagreement has delayed the next board deliberations, with the November 26 meeting postponed to November 30 following Noel's objections over the notice period and circulation of agenda papers. The board is expected to revisit the listing question, the proposed restructuring and the implications of Chandrasekaran's reappointment. Tata Trusts, a collection of charitable trusts, holds about 65.9 per cent of Tata Sons, while the SP Group is the largest minority shareholder. The remaining shares are held largely by Tata Group companies and other shareholders. For the Mistrys, a listing would provide a route to monetise at least part of their substantial investment, subject to applicable restrictions, and reduce their financial exposure. For Tata Trusts, a public offering could alter the group's ownership and governance dynamics, introduce public shareholders and subject the holding company to greater market scrutiny.

articles.title: 'Lotus is the CM face of BJP': Deputy CM Keshav Prasad Maurya says 'leader' to be picked after UP poll results
articles.summary: Uttar Pradesh Deputy Chief Minister Keshav Prasad Maurya on Wednesday said that 'lotus is the CM face' of the BJP in the upcoming Assembly elections in the State. Speaking to reporters in Jaunpur, he said the "leader" will be chosen after the election results are announced. "During an election, the lotus is the face of the BJP. Once the election concludes and the MLAs are elected, the party will hold a meeting. Central observers will arrive, and based on a consensus reached during that meeting, a leader would be chosen," he said. He also said that it was not for him to decide whether incumbent Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath would continue in the post or be replaced by someone else. Uttar Pradesh Dy CM calls SP-Congress alliance 'thug-bandhan', says BJP unaffected by such 'theatrics' "Currently, our Chief Minister is Yogi Adityanath. Whether he will continue as Chief Minister or someone else will take the role is not for me to decide; that will be determined by the MLAs who are elected at that time," he said. Earlier in the day, he dubbedf the SP-Congress alliance “thugbandhan”, an dalleged that the two parties represent criminals, rioters and corrupt elements and claimed that the BJP would form the government in the state after the elections. "That is not an alliance but a 'thugbandhan (alliance of deceivers)’ of goons, criminals, corrupt people and rioters. Its condition is neither good today nor is it going to improve in the future," he said. He appealed to voters to defeat the SP, Congress and their allies and ensure the victory of the BJP-led NDA. Targeting SP president Akhilesh Yadav, Maurya accused him of indulging in political theatrics over issues such as PDA (Picchda, Dalit, Alpsankhyak), visiting Ayodhya and Mathura, and the religious discourse by Bageshwar Dham preacher Dhirendra Krishna Shastri. Shastri recently courted controversy due to one of his speeches where he compared the deities Ram and Krishna. He also accused Yadav of following an anti-Hindu approach. "If we say 'Jai Shri Ram', Akhilesh Yadav should also say 'Jai Shri Ram'. If we say 'Jai Shri Krishna', he should also say 'Jai Shri Krishna'. If we say 'Radhe Radhe, make the lotus bloom', he can say 'Radhe Radhe, puncture the bicycle'," Maurya quipped.

articles.title: Deepam row | 'Most unfortunate': Tamil Nadu govt blames temple board for non-lighting of lamp at Deepathoon
articles.summary: The Tamil Nadu government on Wednesday apologised to the Supreme Court over the failure to light the ceremonial lamp at the disputed Deepathoon pillar on Thirupparankundram hill , blaming the Arulmigu Subramaniaswamy temple authorities for not authorising the team assigned to carry out the exercise. The apology came amid demands for contempt proceedings against the state over alleged willful disobedience of the Supreme Court's November 20 order permitting the lamp to be lit at the pillar on November 24. The Supreme Court, however, refused to initiate suo motu contempt proceedings, asking the petitioners to file a separate plea. A bench of Justices Aravind Kumar and Vipul M Pancholi said the registry would verify the applications filed and explore listing them on Thursday or Friday. Despite the SC's permission to lit the lamp at the stone pillar on the hill, the annual Karthigai Deepam was lit only at its customary Uchipillayar mandapam at Thirupparankundram on Monday. BJP, RSS trying to divide Tamil Nadu over Thirupparankundram deepam row: Manickam Tagore In an interim status report, Madurai District Collector Nishant Krishna said the administration had completed all arrangements to implement the court's order. However, the temple's Board of Trustees did not authorise the proposed 10-member team and instead decided to follow the customary practice of lighting the Karthigai Deepam at its traditional location. The collector maintained that he made every effort to ensure compliance with apex court's order and denied any willful disobedience, while expressing sincere regret over the lamp not being lit at Deepathoon. Appearing for the state, senior advocate Gopal Sankaranarayanan informed the court that the lamp could not be lit at the disputed location. Meanwhile senior advocate Guru Krishnakumar, representing Hindu Dharma Parishad, termed the developments "most unfortunate" and accused the authorities of deliberately circumventing the court's order. The bench, however, declined to initiate contempt proceedings on its own and asked petitioners to file an appropriate separate petition. "No suo motu; file the necessary petition. We will issue appropriate orders, if required. File it, then we will see," Justice Kumar said. The collector's 16-page report detailed several preparatory measures, including meetings held between November 20 and 22, security arrangements, access control and logistical planning. The ceremony was scheduled between 6:00 pm and 6:30 pm on November 24. The temple had proposed temporary scaffolding, protective arrangements around the pillar, electric lighting along the route and a medical team for emergencies. Ten temple functionaries, priests and technical experts were proposed for the ceremony. The administration also sought authorisation for the team from the temple authorities through repeated communications. However, the required approval was not received before the scheduled ceremony. Security arrangements involved 5,797 police personnel, while Executive Magistrates were deployed at 20 locations. Prohibitory orders under Section 163 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita were also imposed from November 23 to November 25 following intelligence inputs about possible mobilisation by groups supporting and opposing the lamp-lighting exercise. Karthigai Deepam row: Scuffle in Thirupparankundram as Hindu outfits stage protest as lamp not lit on 'Deepathoon' The controversy centres on the location and authority for lighting the Karthigai Deepam on Thirupparankundram hill. Traditionally, the lamp has been lit at the Deepa Mandapam near the Uchipillaiyar temple. Hindu groups sought permission to light it at Deepathoon, a stone pillar situated higher up the hill, around 50 metres from the dargah. The dargah side opposed the demand, claiming ownership of the hilltop. Following the Supreme Court's November 20 order allowing the lighting at Deepathoon as a one-time measure, the temple authorities nevertheless lit the lamp only at its customary location. In a statement issued on Tuesday night, the temple's Board of Trustees maintained that long-standing religious traditions must take precedence.

articles.title: The New Aspirational Lifestyle Isn't About Spending More. It's About Planning Better.
articles.summary: For India's working professionals and urban households, financial goals are no longer limited to buying a house or saving for retirement. They also include experiences and lifestyle choices that make everyday life more comfortable and rewarding. But behind many of these aspirations lies a common reality: they are often built around the income of an individual and the responsibilities they carry towards their family. Before planning how future goals will be funded, it is equally important to consider how loved ones would be financially supported if that income were no longer available. As aspirations grow, so does the need to plan for them. A salary may arrive every month, but expenses rarely follow an identical pattern. Travel plans can coincide with annual expenses, a vehicle upgrade may require a sizeable payment, and retirement needs a financial arrangement that can continue long after regular employment ends. This makes it important to build a financial plan that balances two objectives: protecting the people who depend on you and creating a reliable path towards future goals. The challenge is not simply to earn more, but to organise money in a way that offers long-term financial protection while supporting aspirations. India's household spending patterns offer an interesting perspective. According to the Household Consumption Expenditure Survey 2023–24, non-food items accounted for approximately 60% of average monthly per-capita consumption expenditure in urban India . Conveyance contributed 8.46%, miscellaneous goods and entertainment 6.92%, and durable goods 6.87% of total urban consumption expenditure. [1] These categories reflect how household budgets extend beyond essential food expenditure to mobility, entertainment and purchases that support everyday living. For someone planning a lifestyle upgrade, the important question is not just how much it will cost today, but how the money will be available when the goal arrives. This is where predictable financial inflows can become useful. The first step is to separate aspirations into goals that are fixed and those that are flexible. A planned retirement date, a home purchase or a major family commitment may have a specific timeline and funding requirement. A holiday, a vehicle upgrade or a technology purchase may allow some flexibility in timing or amount. Once the difference is clear, planning becomes more focused. Instead of trying to predict what markets, interest rates or prices will do several years from now, individuals can concentrate on the factors within their control: the amount they want to plan for, the date by which they need it, and how certain the funding must be. Market-linked options can play a role in a broader financial plan, but for goals where a defined benefit is important, guaranteed*-benefit solutions[1] offer another approach. What does a predictable payout bring to financial planning? Predictable payouts bring clarity to planning, knowing exactly what amount will be available, and when, makes it easier to connect money with a specific life moment. Depending on the selected option, the benefit can be received as a one-time lump sum or as regular income. This can make it easier to plan for a particular milestone. Someone preparing for a home purchase may prefer a lump sum around the intended purchase period. Another person may want regular income to support a planned lifestyle or a future retirement routine. The objective is to match the payout structure to the purpose of the money. The plan can help individuals planning personal goals such as buying a home, purchasing a vehicle or preparing for retirement. It offers guaranteed benefits, which can be aligned to either a lump sum or regular income, depending on what the goal requires. The idea is not to make every lifestyle choice dependent on a financial product. It is to give important goals a clearer funding strategy along with financial protection for the loved ones. A planned holiday, a vehicle purchase or a retirement income requirement may each need a different approach. Some goals can accommodate uncertainty, while others benefit from knowing the amount and timing of the expected payout. Ultimately, financial planning in a changing world is less about predicting every development and more about making deliberate choices. The economy may change, prices may move and priorities may evolve. But individuals can still decide what they are working towards, when they need the money and how they want to receive it. Aspirations evolve with time- having clarity on how they’ll be funded makes the journey smoother. Documenting a Student Space-Payload Project: Lessons from Blue Blocks
articles.summary: On 12 January 2026, ISRO's PSLV-C62 lifted off from the Satish Dhawan Space Centre at Sriharikota carrying a set of small payloads alongside its main mission. One of them, a thermal sensor payload called SBB-1, had been designed and built by 17 students aged 12 to 16 from Blue Blocks Montessori School in Hyderabad. Minutes into the flight, the rocket's third stage suffered an anomaly, and all of the payloads on board were lost. What remains of SBB-1 is not in orbit. It is in a record: an authorisation from India's space regulator, qualification test results, a published mission document and the students' own design files. For a school, that record may turn out to be the most valuable thing the project produced. Not a satellite launch: what SBB-1 actually was Search results for a student satellite program in India tend to blur an important distinction. SBB-1 was not a standalone satellite. It was a hosted payload: a self-contained instrument that travels on a larger spacecraft, known as the host, which provides power, communication and a ride to orbit. The payload was built to the dimensions of a 1U CubeSat, a cube 10 centimetres on each side, and its instrument was a multi-point thermal sensor array designed to measure temperature at several points in space. The host spacecraft was the MOI-1 bus, operated by the Indian space-technology company TakeMe2Space, which acted as the project's technical integration partner. The hosted model suits a school project well. Because the host spacecraft supplies power, communication and the ride to orbit, a student team can concentrate on the instrument itself: what it should measure, how it should be built and how to prove it will survive. It also means the students work alongside professional engineers on the parts of a mission that would be beyond a school's resources, learning how a real space project divides its responsibilities. What is CubeSat and how do students build it? A CubeSat is a standardised small spacecraft format, built from units of 10 by 10 by 10 centimetres. Because the size and interfaces are standard, CubeSats and CubeSat-format payloads can be designed, tested and launched far more affordably than conventional spacecraft, which is why universities, start-ups and, increasingly, schools use them. Building one is less about assembling parts than about meeting requirements. Students define what the instrument should measure, choose components that can survive launch and space, design and assemble the circuit board, and then prove through testing that the hardware will work. At Blue Blocks, the students designed and assembled the payload's circuit board themselves. The finished hardware then passed a series of qualification tests at approved facilities: thermal vacuum cycling between minus 20 and plus 60 degrees Celsius, random vibration testing to ISRO specifications, and electromagnetic compatibility and structural checks. The paper trail: how the project was documented Every stage of SBB-1 left a document behind, and that is the part of the project other schools can learn most from. The authorisation. Any activity in space by a non-government entity in India requires approval from IN-SPACe, the Indian National Space Promotion and Authorization Centre. SBB-1 received authorisation PMA/IN-SPACe/AUTH/2026/115, issued to Blue Blocks Montessori Educational Society for the establishment and operation of the SBB-1 hosted payload. Under it, the Society accepted legal responsibility under the international conventions on liability and registration that govern objects in space. The registrations. The payload was entered in the Department of Space master registry in December 2025, and a radio-frequency filing was made with the International Telecommunication Union through the host operator. The division of roles. The project ran on a three-part structure: the student team handled design, development and testing; Blue Blocks Micro Research Institute provided pedagogical and regulatory guidance; and TakeMe2Space provided the technical architecture, hardware validation and launch integration. Writing that structure down at the start meant that every decision could later be traced to whoever made it. The mission record. After the launch, the project was written up and archived as Valorization in Orbit: An Adolescent CubeSat Mission (January 2026), alongside the authorisation itself, which is published with a permanent identifier. An overview of the project is available on the Blue Blocks SBB-1 project page. "When the rocket failed, the first question from the students was not whether we would try again, but what we had recorded," says Pavan Goyal, Founder of Blue Blocks. "That told me the project had done its job. A launch lasts a few minutes. A well-kept record lasts long enough for the next team to build on it." What is the Blue Blocks Space Program? The space programme at Blue Blocks sits within the school's adolescent years, from Classes 7 to 10, at its Tellapur campus. It treats space not as a topic but as a working environment with real rules: orbital mechanics, power budgets, telemetry, regulatory approval and the responsibility of putting an object into a shared orbit. Students learn the science through the demands of an actual mission rather than a textbook chapter. The wider student space learning programme is run through the school's space lab. The students who built SBB-1 have not left the project behind. They are now mentoring a younger team working on a second payload, SBB-2, which the school is working towards for 2027. The design files, test results and lessons from SBB-1 are the starting point for that work, which is exactly what a documented project makes possible. "It was a hard morning for the children, and for all of us," says Munira Hussain Kagalwalla, Co-founder and Director of Blue Blocks. "But within a week they were back in the lab, going through the test data line by line. Watching them turn disappointment into a plan for SBB-2 was one of the proudest moments we have had as a school." The benefits of space programs in schools The case for a school with a space program in India is sometimes made in terms of inspiration alone. SBB-1 suggests the benefits are more concrete, and most of them do not depend on the launch succeeding. Working to a real standard. A payload that must pass vibration and thermal vacuum tests cannot be "nearly right". Students learn what a specification is, and why it matters, in a way no classroom exercise can replicate. Seeing a whole system. A thermal sensor is useless without power, data handling and a host spacecraft to carry it. Students learn that every part depends on every other, and that a design decision in one place has consequences somewhere else. Understanding responsibility. Few school projects involve a government authorisation and international treaty obligations. Learning that space is regulated, shared and governed by law gives students a very different sense of what engineering involves. Learning to document. Perhaps the most transferable skill of all. Engineers, scientists and researchers spend a large part of their working lives recording what they did and why. SBB-1's students learnt that habit under real conditions, with real consequences. How the research institute supports projects like this Projects on this scale need more than enthusiasm. At Blue Blocks, the Blue Blocks micro research institute provides the framework that turns student work into a usable record: guidance on regulatory processes, standards for how observations and data are kept, and a route to publishing outcomes with permanent identifiers so that others can find and cite them. For SBB-1, the institute's role was to make sure that whatever happened on launch day, the knowledge the students built would not be lost with the hardware. A school with a space lab in Hyderabad The space lab is based at the school's Tellapur campus, where it sits alongside drone, biomimicry and innovation labs as part of a wider innovation curriculum. For families looking for a school with an innovation curriculum in Hyderabad, the distinctive feature is that these labs are not separate from the rest of the school day. They are where the adolescent years' academic work is put to use on problems with real stakes. Lessons for any school attempting this For schools and educators considering a student space project of their own, SBB-1 offers three practical lessons. Start the paperwork on the first day. Regulatory approval, registration and frequency filing take time, and the documents produced along the way are part of the learning, not a distraction from it. Define roles in writing. A clear division between students, mentors and the technical partner protects the integrity of the students' work and makes every decision traceable later. Plan for the outcome you cannot control. Launch failures happen to national space agencies, not only to schools. A project designed to leave behind a complete record still has value when the rocket does not reach orbit, and gives the next team somewhere to begin. The students who built SBB-1 learnt that lesson in the hardest way possible. In 2027, the team working on SBB-2 will begin with everything they recorded. Frequently Asked Questions What is the difference between a student satellite and a hosted payload? A standalone satellite requires its own power, propulsion, and communication systems. A hosted payload (like SBB-1) is a self-contained instrument that hitches a ride on a larger professional spacecraft. This allows students to focus entirely on designing the instrument and analyzing data, rather than building the entire spacecraft infrastructure. How do students test a space payload before launch? Before IN-SPACe grants authorization, the hardware must survive rigorous qualification testing at approved facilities. Students must prove their payload can withstand extreme thermal vacuum cycling (from -20°C to +60°C), intense launch vibrations, and electromagnetic compatibility checks to ensure it won't interfere with the host spacecraft. Why is documentation so important for a student space mission? A rocket launch can fail in minutes, but proper documentation ensures the educational value survives. By archiving design files, qualification test results, and regulatory authorizations with permanent identifiers, students learn how professional engineers record their work, and future teams have a blueprint for their own missions. What happens if the rocket carrying a student payload fails? Launch anomalies are a reality of space exploration. When the PSLV-C62 mission was lost, the Blue Blocks students used their archived data and test results to immediately begin designing a successor payload, SBB-2. The failure provided a masterclass in engineering resilience and the critical importance of a well-kept mission record.

articles.title: Beyond the battlefield: How security agencies are digging into Jammu and Kashmir’s old terror networks
articles.summary: Srinagar: More than three decades after militancy took root in Jammu and Kashmir , security agencies are revisiting old cases, tracing cross-border militants and targeting suspected terror-financing networks. In the latest instance, the police have identified 30 men from the Reasi district who allegedly went missing between 1991 and 2003 before crossing over to Pakistan for arms and ammunition training. The investigation has also led to action against properties belonging to five alleged Pakistan-based militants from the district. Police suspect that they were attempting to sell the land to finance terrorist activities. The five have been identified as Mohd Qayoom alias Abdul Qayoom of Shadole, Bashir Ahmad alias Masoom of Bidder, Shokat Ali of Hunder, Manzoor Ahmad alias Manzoor Hussain of Khanti and Imtiyaz Ahmad of Thuroo. Jammu and Kashmir: SIA likely to take up more decades-old terror-killing cases The properties together measure approximately 29 kanals (3.6 acres) with Manzoor Ahmad owning the largest share of 15 kanals and 19 marlas (almost 2 acres). Director General of Police (DGP) Nalin Prabhat granted approval for attachment under Section 25 of the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act (UAPA), treating the properties as proceeds of terrorism under Section 2(1)(g)(ii) of the Act. According to an order issued by the Jammu and Kashmir Police Headquarters on November 19, Mahore Police Station received information on November 29, 2024, that 30 people from Mahore and Chassana police jurisdictions had gone missing between 1991 and 2003 and crossed over to Pakistan for arms and ammunition training. Police allege that the men are now working for Hizbul Mujahideen from Pakistan, supplying weapons, ammunition and money to sponsor terrorism and attempting to radicalise and recruit local youth. 30 missing terrorists from Reasi exfiltrated to Pakistan for arms training: DGP Nalin Prabhat The Reasi investigation is part of a wider effort by security agencies to pursue old militancy-related cases. In Kupwara, police initiated proceedings in 2024 to attach properties of 51 alleged terror handlers operating from Pakistan-occupied Kashmir, several of whom had been declared proclaimed offenders by courts. In January 2025, properties of 11 alleged Pakistan-based militants from Kishtwar were attached following court orders. The State Investigation Agency (SIA) has also revisited several decades-old cases involving targeted killings of Kashmiri Pandits. These include the 1998 Wandhama massacre, in which 23 Kashmiri Pandits were killed, and the murders of BJP leader Tika Lal Taploo and writer Sarwanand Koul Premi. In June 2026, the SIA filed a chargesheet in the 1990 murder of Kashmiri Pandit nurse Sarla Bhat, naming five alleged Jammu and Kashmir Liberation Front operatives, including its chief Yasin Malik. In another instance, police arrested two suspects in August 2026 in connection with the 1991 Jammu railway station bombing, which killed three people and injured 18. The investigations involve tracing suspects, examining old records and reconstructing links in cases that remained unresolved for decades.

articles.title: RV Educational Institutions Appoints Rajat Patidar as Brand Ambassador to Champion Student Leadership and Resilience
articles.summary: RV Educational Institutions (RVEI) has appointed Indian cricketer and Royal Challengers Bengaluru (RCB) captain Rajat Patidar as its brand ambassador. The association, themed “The Pursuit of Excellence”, aims to encourage students across RVEI’s 28 institutions to develop the perseverance, self-belief and sense of responsibility needed to pursue their ambitions in education and beyond. For RVEI, the partnership is an opportunity to make the idea of excellence more meaningful to students, beyond examination results or individual achievements. Through institutional communications and student engagement initiatives, the group intends to highlight how young people can respond to setbacks, recognise opportunities, build confidence and put their abilities to purposeful use. This aligns with RVEI’s guiding philosophy, “Go, Change the World”, which encourages students to connect ambition with responsibility and real-world contribution. Patidar’s journey offers a relatable example of those values. After returning to RCB as an injury replacement in 2022, he scored an unbeaten 112 in an IPL Eliminator, later represented India and was named RCB captain in 2025. Under his leadership, the franchise won its first IPL title in 2025 and retained the championship in 2026. RVEI sees the discipline, resilience and leadership behind this progression, rather than the sporting milestones alone, as the connection to its educational mission. Mr. Nikhil A. Space Engineering and Technology: 500 BTech seats, 300 master's seats and 200 PhD seats, taking the total to 1,000. Overall, the initiative will include 3,000 BTech seats, 1,500 master's seats and 1,500 PhD seats . The Robotics and Physical AI programmes will combine mechanical and electrical engineering with software, machine learning, computer vision, sensing and control systems. Students will work on both hardware and software, with research areas including humanoid and legged robots, swarm robotics, soft robotics, foundation models and digital twins. The programmes will focus on applications in healthcare, defense, agriculture and industrial manufacturing. The curriculum is also expected to include industry-linked projects and a paid industry-residency semester. It will focus on areas such as satellite navigation, space robotics and human spaceflight. The programmes are expected to prepare students for specialised work in space engineering and technology, including the development of systems for space exploration and satellite applications. The foundation has not yet named the IITs that will participate in the new initiative or identified the institute that will host the proposed School of Space Science and Technology. articles.title: Tamil Nadu signs MoUs worth Rs 58,000 crore generating 65,000 jobs at Chennai conclave
articles.summary: Chennai: At the second investors' conclave within 200 days of the TVK dispensation assuming office, the Tamil Nadu government on Wednesday signed MoUs with 78 companies, which pledged investments totaling Rs 58,214 crore, generating 65,786 jobs. Hosur, located just outside Bengaluru, and Krishnagiri district secured about 13 projects worth Rs 12,643 crore, creating 14,600 jobs. These investments span sectors ranging from electronics and two-wheeler manufacturing to automobile components and semiconductors. Significant investments in Krishnagiri district include Titan Company pledging Rs 1,500 crore to manufacture precision components for the aerospace, semiconductor, and defence sectors, and Rs 2,000 crore by TVS Motor Company for expanding its two-wheeler manufacturing unit in Hosur. Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay , who oversaw the signing of the MoUs, also laid the foundation for several projects, including the manufacturing unit of electric scooter manufacturer Ultraviolette in Krishnagiri district. BJP, RSS trying to divide Tamil Nadu over Thirupparankundram deepam row: Manickam Tagore The investment pledges came even as the Tamil Nadu government fights a perception that it is losing key investments to neighbouring Andhra Pradesh. A massive controversy broke out last week alleging that Guidance, the investment promotion arm of the Tamil Nadu government, faced “mass resignations” after the TVK assumed office. Employees were reportedly asked to resign following allegations that “sensitive information” was leaked to the Andhra Pradesh Economic Development Board (APEDB). articles.title: Rare 'intensive' revision in Bihar four months before polls
articles.summary: The Election Commission's 'Special Intensive Revision' of Bihar's electoral rolls has ignited political debate, differing from past revisions. While intensive revisions aren't new, the timing of Bihar's SIR, months before assembly elections, is unusual. Unlike previous 'de novo' exercises, it builds upon the 2002-03 roll, incorporating new enumeration forms and document submission.

articles.title: Lok Sabha election 2024: Maharashtra get interesting after splits in Shiv Sena, NCP
articles.summary: Lok Sabha election 2024: ​​The BJP-Shiv Sena won 41 of the 48 seats in the 2019 polls, but the Sena has split since and a vast majority of the Bal Thackeray-founded party is now allied with the BJP. The Nationalist Congress Party also split as well with Ajit Pawar joining the ruling alliance in the state, led by Eknath Shinde. In the 2019 Lok Sabha polls, the BJP emerged the top party with 23 seats, followed by the undivided Sena with 18.

articles.title: Implementation of 'guarantees', decline of BRS favour Congress in Telangana, BJP aiming for better show
articles.summary: The BJP, riding high on its growing voter base in Telangana, is now aiming to win over 12 out of the total 17 seats and 35 per cent vote share, in the upcoming Lok Sabha polls. The party doubled its vote share to nearly 14 per cent resulting in eight seats in the assembly elections held on November 30, last year. BRS, which ruled the state for about a decade since its emergence, is low on morale following the defeat, even as its founder and former Chief Minister K Chandrasekhar Rao's daughter K Kavitha was arrested on the eve of poll dates announcement, adding insult to the injury.
